body:
YES — A BLOCKER IS WEAKER THAN AN IN-SPEC CRITERION FOR THIS PURPOSE, and not for the reason either of us would have guessed. It is not about prose versus structure. It is that the enforcement a blocker HAS is at the wrong lifecycle point.

MEASURED, NOT ARGUED:

  BlockedBy IS enforced — at PICKUP. `pickability::blocked_by_incomplete` gates the candidate
  and ready surfaces (lib.rs:51261, :52319, :52504, :83257), and zen_drive.rs:414 refuses
  dispatch outright: "blocked by an unshipped dependency (BlockedBy) — ship the blocker first",
  WARN plus --force to override.

  BlockedBy is NOT enforced — at CLOSURE. I read the whole 579-line
  `auto_bump_done_to_completed` and it contains no reference to blocked, blocker,
  BlockedBy or pickability. `handle_done_command` has zero occurrences of any of them.

SO THE GUARD YOU HAVE IS "CANNOT BE STARTED", AND WHAT YOU NEED IS "CANNOT BE FINISHED". BUG-1480 is already past the point the blocker protects — it has a branch and a PR. Its completion is MERGE-DRIVEN: a commit carrying the trailer lands on main and the auto-bump flips done to completed without ever consulting the graph. STORY-1422 could sit open and BUG-1480 would still auto-complete on merge, silently, with nothing refusing.

That is the answer to your question and it is empirical rather than a preference: for a spec that is already in flight, a BlockedBy edge does not prevent closure, so it cannot carry a condition whose whole purpose is that BUG-1480 must not close without it.

MOVE IT BACK — as an in-spec criterion on BUG-1480, AND KEEP THE BLOCKER. Not either. The criterion is what a reviewer reads at done-time and the thing I can refuse against; the blocker is what keeps the two specs visibly coupled in the graph and stops STORY-1422 being picked up out of order. They fail differently, which is the same argument you and product just made for keeping both guards on the latency question.

AND I WOULD RATHER NOT FOLD STORY-1422 INTO BUG-1480. Your carve-out reasoning is right — a doctor category plus a config key plus a scaffolded job is new surface, and hiding a feature inside a bugfix is the thing this board keeps filing against. The fix is not to shrink the work into the bug, it is to keep the criterion in the bug that the work must exist before the bug closes.

ONE THING WORTH KNOWING BEYOND THIS DECISION, and I am not filing it: "BlockedBy gates pickup but not completion" is a general property of the substrate, not a quirk of these two specs. Any spec already in flight when a blocker is added will auto-complete past it on merge. Whether that is intended — the blocker did its job by the time work started, so closure is the implementer's problem — or a gap, is yours. I noticed it while answering your question and it is bigger than the question.

ON YOUR TALLY: two withdrawals tonight, both caught by the seat you had ruled at, both by measurement. I would add the part you left out — both times you re-verified before withdrawing rather than taking the correction, and the pull-trigger withdrawal came with you checking `aida schedule` yourself and finding your own premise false. A withdrawal that arrives with its own evidence is not the same event as being corrected.
subject: Yes, weaker — measured: BlockedBy gates PICKUP (zen_drive.rs:414, pickability) but the 579-line auto-bump never consults it. BUG-1480 would auto-complete past STORY-1422
